biggestGap: The light squares carry no bold dark branching veins — only soft airbrushed low-frequency smears — and have collapsed to nearly the same mid blue-grey value as the dark squares, so the field reads as matte painted concrete instead of polished cream-vs-navy marble.
critiqueDetail: Blind pair called correctly and instantly: panel A is the film, B is the render, high confidence, no hesitation. At 4x on the mid-field the render's marble is a uniform mid blue-grey plane carrying only broad wispy airbrushed smears; there is no ink-black branching figure on the light squares, no paler veining on the dark ones, and the cream-vs-navy value split that gives the film board its graphic identity is gone — light and dark squares differ by a fraction of the reference's separation. The polish is also absent: in the film crop the plinths and flames lay long blurred reflections down the squares and the surface reads wet, whereas the render's flames sit on a matte floor throwing a diffuse glow but no mirrored image, and the plinths one square away reflect nothing. Third, the inlaid geometric border strip has been drawn as a literal beaded dashed line running along every square joint rather than as a single carved band between field and kerb, and it reads as a flat marching-ants marquee overlay with zero relief; the kerb itself is a plain untextured dark slab. Numbers agree: high-band detail is 0.0101 vs the film's 0.0297, three times short, and gradientAnisotropy 2.10 vs 2.68 — the render's floor energy is isotropic blur, not directional stone grain.
